transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Orion Infra), Diego Alvarez (Orion Cloud Architect), Priya Menon (Orion Security), Connor Lee (Orion DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, constraints and success criteria, deep dive on connectivity choices (peering vs private endpoints), region constraints (eu-west-1 vs us-west-2), KMS/encryption questions, next steps and pilot plan.

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about an hour, we'll do intros real quick and then Ravi will walk through the network options.
[00:12] Maya (Orion): Yep thanks, Maya here - infra manager. We want to make sure we can keep traffic off the public internet for PII workloads, basically private-only.
[00:20] Diego (Orion): Diego - cloud arch; our main constraints are multi-region failover, CIDR overlap across some older VPCs, and egress firewall policy that logs to our SIEM.
[00:27] Ava: Great — same page. Ravi, over to you?
[00:31] Ravi (Redwood SE): Sure — hi all. I'll outline three patterns: 1) direct VPC peering to Redwood Private VPCs, 2) AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints to a private service endpoint, 3) transit-gw style hub-and-spoke. We'll cover tradeoffs.
[00:45] Lina (Redwood): quick note, we also recommend a prefix/KV cache-friendly setup on the runtime side but network first.
[01:02] Diego: Quick question — if we go PrivateLink, do we need to handle cross-account endpoint management? We have multiple AWS accounts per team.
[01:12] Ravi: Yeah PrivateLink requires interface endpoints in each account or cross-account configurations. It tends to be simpler for overlapping CIDR because it doesn't require peering route table edits, but there's per-interface ENI egress and IP management.
[01:29] Connor (Orion): And what about throughput and latency? This is for low-latency inference (sub-50ms target).
[01:36] Ravi: Good point. VPC peering gives you native routing and tends to be slightly lower latency. PrivateLink adds an extra hop, small bump, but it's usually within acceptable bounds for many customers. We can run bench tests from your infra to quantify.
[01:54] Priya (Orion): From security side, we need control plane logs and KMS envelope for keys. Do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logs tied back to our SIEM?
[02:05] Ava: Yes, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we ship audit logs. I'll send our SOC2 and a short security FAQ after this call.
[02:13] Speaker 1: (garbled) also if you want SAML...
[02:19] Maya: We use SSO via Okta, need SAML/SAML2 SSO and RBAC mapping.
[02:26] Lina: We support SAML SSO for the control plane; RBAC can be mapped to groups. For the runtime data plane, auth is network-level plus token-based.
[02:38] Diego: Region question: our primary workloads are in eu-west-1 but backups/usability in us-west-2. Does Redwood Private support multi-region deployment or do we need separate Private instances per region?
[02:51] Ravi: Right now, deployments are region-bound. For low-latency you can run dedicated instances in both regions; we can discuss replication and failover patterns. Many customers deploy in primary and warm-standby in a second region.
[03:06] Diego: So we'd need two Private deployments, and then decide routing / egress.
[03:11] Ava: That's the typical pattern. We can also route requests to hosted fallbacks but that may hit data residency concerns.
[03:19] Priya: Egress constraints — our compliance team requires all egress to be funneled through approved NAT + inline DLP. Can that be enforced with PrivateLink or peering?
[03:31] Ravi: With VPC peering, your egress flows like any VPC destination. You can control it with route tables and NAT. With PrivateLink, the interface endpoints are ENIs in your VPC so you can still apply security group rules and egress controls. Transit gateway gives centralized control if you want a hub.
[03:47] Maya: Do we need to open ports to public IPs for healthchecks? That was a pain with another vendor.
[03:54] Lina: For Private deployments, healthchecks are internal — we don't require opening public endpoints. If you use the Hosted API you'd need secure egress.
[04:02] Ava: quick housekeeping — we'll attach a recommended terraform snippet for PrivateLink and a sample peering template.
[04:10] Diego: About CIDR overlap — some older VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16 and several teams conflict. Transit-gw seems heavy; is NAT with asymmetric routes an option?
[04:22] Ravi: You can use a central transit with NAT translation (AWS TGW with route table transformations) if you need to avoid overlap, or use an application layer gateway in the middle. PrivateLink avoids the issue by using interface endpoints.
[04:38] Connor: Cost: any rough delta between peering vs PrivateLink vs transit? We have to feed finance an estimate.
[04:45] Ava: Ballpark — peering is low network cost but operational overhead at scale; PrivateLink has per-GB and per-hour ENI costs; transit gateway adds hourly attachment costs but centralizes routing. We'll send a cost comparison by next steps.
[04:58] Maya: Ok that's helpful. Also we're evaluating Dedicated (reserved) vs Private. For Dedicated, do we get single-tenant GPUs but still managed network?
[05:07] Ravi: Dedicated is dedicated capacity in our infra but still managed by Redwood; you can pair it with Private deployment for VPC isolation. Private is where the control plane is customer-managed in VPC.
[05:18] Priya: Data retention: logs for inference payloads — can we set retention and ensure logs don't leave region?
[05:26] Ava: Yes, retention is configurable and with Private you can keep audit logs in your S3 within the region. We'll document defaults.
[05:33] Speaker 2: (mumble) also encryption at rest?
[05:37] Lina: AES-256 default, and we can plug in customer-managed KMS keys for both runtime and control plane metadata.
[05:44] Diego: Any latency guarantees in SLA for Private deployments?
[05:49] Ravi: SLAs typically cover uptime. Latency SLOs are configured by instance type and queue depth. For the pilot we recommend a small benchmark plan to set realistic SLOs.
[05:58] Ava: Let's talk pilot: we propose a 2-week pilot in eu-west-1 using PrivateLink to start (avoids CIDR refactor), run a latency/cost baseline, then switch to peering for a direct compare if you prefer.
[06:12] Maya: That sounds pragmatic. What do we need to prepare?
[06:15] Ravi: We'll need a small test VPC and credentials for a read-only IAM role to run short tests, plus a list of CIDRs and preferred regions. We'll also share terraform so you can review inline.
[06:27] Connor: Onboarding: are there manual steps that require Redwood action or can we do IaC only?
[06:32] Lina: Most steps can be IaC. There are a couple account-link steps for Private control plane handshake that require a one-time accept by your org admin. We'll note those in the doc.
[06:44] Diego: When you say 'handshake' — is that a cross-account role? We have strict least-privilege rules.
[06:50] Ravi: It's a scoped cross-account role with explicit permission we provide; you can review it before we request. It only allows lifecycle actions for the Private control plane.
[06:58] Priya: We'll want to run an internal pen-test against the staging instance. Is that allowed?
[07:04] Ava: Yes, we allow pentests with advance notice and a scope doc. We'll include the standard pen-test checklist.
[07:10] Maya: Ok, timeline: we want pilot in Nov and a production decision by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
[07:16] Ava: Totally reasonable. Pilot kickoff week of Nov 2 was proposed earlier. If pilot goes well, you can move to Dedicated or full Private in Q1.
[07:24] Diego: One more — egress monitoring. We need flow logs integrated into our SIEM. How do you surface logs?
[07:31] Lina: We publish flow logs and audit logs to an S3 bucket you control; they can be pushed to your SIEM via existing connectors. We'll include sample CloudWatch -> S3 -> SIEM mapping.
[07:42] Speaker 1: (overlap) also, can you do granular network policies?
[07:46] Ravi: Security groups + network ACLs on ENIs, plus application-level tokens. For cross-account PrivateLink there are also allowed principals.
[07:54] Ava: We're getting low on time; quick recap and owners: Ava will send SOC2 and network diagram by 10/25; Ravi will send terraform snippets and peering vs privatelink cost comparison by 10/26; Diego/Connor will provide CIDRs and preferred regions by 10/29; we'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of Nov 2.
[08:15] Maya: Sounds good. Appreciate the clarity.
[08:20] Diego: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:23] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[08:26] (call ends)

Notes: Some transcript lines labeled 'Speaker 1/2' where auto-attribution failed. Occasional filler words and small transcription errors (e.g., 'prefix/KV cache' heard as 'prefix key cache'). Links referenced: Security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security/orion-pack), Terraform snippet repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/privatelink-examples).
